title: Finite-free projection formula
statement:
For $F=\Lambda^N[a]$, the maps $\pi_{h,E,F}$ and $\rho_{h,E,F}$ are inverse:

$$
\rho_{h,E,F}\pi_{h,E,F}=1,\qquad
\pi_{h,E,F}\rho_{h,E,F}=1.
$$

proof.text: Write $R$ for the target ring sheaf (the $\Lambda$ of the statement), $S$ for the source ring sheaf, and use the ringed-topos morphism $h$ and $E\in D(S)$ of [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows]. Let $N\in\mathbf N$, $a\in\mathbf Z$, and give $F=R^{\oplus N}[a]$ the identity splitting in its only nonzero degree $r=-a$. Use the K-injective representative $I$ and chain models $A=h_*I$, $C=\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_R F)$, $J=\operatorname{Tot}(I\otimes_S h^*F)$, $B=h_*J$ specified in that definition. These represent the source and target of $\pi$ and $\rho$. In total degree $n$ there is only the coefficient degree $r=-a$, so $C^n=(h_*I^{n+a})^{\oplus N}$ and $B^n=h_*((I^{n+a})^{\oplus N})$. The coefficient differential is zero; both total differentials are induced by $d_I^{n+a}$, by [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. This description avoids assuming, without a sign calculation, that the right adjoint commutes with shifts.

source.place: ## Proof, finite-free identifications and componentwise identities, expanded below

proof.text: The pulled-back basis maps satisfy $h^*(\mathrm{pr}_i)h^*(\iota_j)=\delta_{ij}$ and $\sum_jh^*(\iota_j)h^*(\mathrm{pr}_j)=1$ by additivity. Moreover $h^*R=S\otimes_{h^{-1}R}h^{-1}R\cong S$ by multiplication, with inverse $s\mapsto s\otimes1$. Thus these maps identify $h^*(R^{\oplus N})$ with $S^{\oplus N}$, also for $N=0$. For an $S$-module sheaf $M$, the ordinary tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] identifies $h^*(h_*M\otimes_R R^{\oplus N})$ with $(h^*h_*M)^{\oplus N}$. The adjunct $t_{M,R^{\oplus N}}$ of the direct sum of $N$ counits has, after composing with $h_*$ of the $j$th projection, the $j$th projection $(h_*M)^{\oplus N}\to h_*M$: the termwise adjunction bijection in [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] sends $\varepsilon_M\circ h^*(\mathrm{pr}_j)$ to $\mathrm{pr}_j$. Thus $t_{M,R^{\oplus N}}$ is the inverse of the product comparison $k_M:h_*(M^{\oplus N})\to(h_*M)^{\oplus N}$. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-limits] applies to the finite discrete category with $N$ objects. Finite module sums are products: the coordinate maps satisfy $\mathrm{pr}_i\iota_j=\delta_{ij}$ and $\sum_j\iota_j\mathrm{pr}_j=1$, as checked sectionwise. Hence $k_M$ is an isomorphism, including when $N=0$. In the notation of the arrow definition, $q_{M,N}=k_M$, and $q_{M,N}t_{M,R^{\oplus N}}=1=t_{M,R^{\oplus N}}q_{M,N}$.

source.place: ## Proof, finite-free identifications and componentwise identities, expanded below

proof.text: Apply Step 2 to $M=I^{n+a}$. Define $t^n=t_{I^{n+a},R^{\oplus N}}$ and $s^n=q_{I^{n+a},N}$. Naturality of the counit in [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] and of the tensor comparison gives $B(d_I)t^n=t^{n+1}C(d_I)$. Multiplication by $s^{n+1}$ on the left and $s^n$ on the right gives $s^{n+1}B(d_I)=C(d_I)s^n$. These are exactly the two chain-map equations since $d_F=0$: in the total differential $d_I\otimes1+(-1)^{n+a}1\otimes d_F$ the second term vanishes. Thus $t:C\to B$ and $s:B\to C$ are inverse chain maps, with $s^nt^n=1$ and $t^ns^n=1$ in every degree.

source.place: ## Proof, finite-free identifications and componentwise identities, expanded below

proof.text: To identify $Qt$ with the particular derived morphism $\pi$, take a K-flat resolution with flat terms $v:P\to A$ from [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The complexes $F$ and $P\otimes F$ are K-flat: tensoring an acyclic test complex with $F$ gives a reindexed finite sum of that complex, and tensoring it with $P\otimes F$ gives a reindexed finite sum of its acyclic tensor with $P$, by [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Acyclicity here is checked by coordinate kernels and images; the standard shift signs are removed by multiplying degree $n$ by $(-1)^{an}$. Terms of $P\otimes F$ are finite sums of flat terms of $P$, hence flat since tensor exactness can be checked coordinatewise. In degree $n$ the map $v\otimes1:C_P=P\otimes F\to C$ is $(v^{n+a})^{\oplus N}$ and the differentials are $(d^{n+a})^{\oplus N}$. Hence its map on degree-$n$ cohomology is $(H^{n+a}(v))^{\oplus N}$, an isomorphism, so it is a quasi-isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], $h^*(P\otimes F)=h^*P\otimes h^*F$ represents $Lh^*(Rh_*E\otimes_R^L F)$ with the canonical tensor comparison. Apply [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] to the ordinary module adjunction and its canonical derived adjunction specified by the arrow definition. For that formula take $M=C_P$, $K=J$, and both quasi-isomorphisms $t$ and $s$ to be identities. The cone map $u_{1_{C_P}}:Lh^*(QC_P)\to Qh^*C_P$ and cocone map $p_{1_J}:Qh_*J\to Rh_*(QJ)$ are the representative isomorphisms: $C_P$ has K-flat flat terms and $J$ is K-injective by the arrow definition. Essential constancy is provided by the canonical total derived operations stipulated there. Thus its representative formula, under precisely these isomorphisms, says that $Q(t\circ(v\otimes1))$ has adjunct the localization of $h^*P\otimes h^*F\xrightarrow{h^*v\otimes1}h^*h_*I\otimes h^*F\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_I\otimes1}I\otimes h^*F$. Taking $M=P$, $K=I$, $s=t=1$ in that formula, with their K-flat and K-injective representative isomorphisms, sends $Qv:QP\to Qh_*I=Rh_*E$ to $Q(\varepsilon_I\circ h^*v)$; since $Qv$ is the source representative identification, this is the derived counit $\varepsilon_E$ under that identification. Consequently the first displayed adjunct is $\varepsilon_E\otimes1$ after the canonical derived tensor comparison. This is precisely the defining adjunct of $\pi$ in [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows]. Bijectivity of the derived adjunction and cancellation of the isomorphism $Q(v\otimes1)$ give $Qt=\pi_{h,E,F}$.

source.place: ## Proof, finite-free identifications and componentwise identities, expanded below

proof.text: The identity splitting of the only coefficient term makes the formula for $s_{n+a,-a}$ in [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows] exactly $q_{I^{n+a},N}$; thus the definition of $\rho$ as the localization of the finite-total chain map gives $Qs=\rho_{h,E,F}$. Applying the localization functor to the chain equalities $st=1$ and $ts=1$ of Step 3 preserves compositions and identities. With $Qt=\pi$ from Step 4 these are $\rho_{h,E,F}\pi_{h,E,F}=1$ and $\pi_{h,E,F}\rho_{h,E,F}=1$.
